claims.text: In 2012, suboptimal intake of 10 dietary factors was associated with an estimated 318,656 cardiometabolic deaths (45.4% of total) among US adults.
High sodium intake was associated with the highest number of estimated diet-related cardiometabolic deaths in 2012, accounting for 66,508 deaths (9.5%).
Low intake of nuts and seeds was associated with 59,374 cardiometabolic deaths (8.5%) in 2012.
High intake of processed meats was associated with 57,766 cardiometabolic deaths (8.2%) in 2012.
Between 2002 and 2012, population-adjusted US cardiometabolic deaths per year decreased by 26.5%.
Between 2002 and 2012, the greatest decline in diet-related cardiometabolic deaths was associated with insufficient polyunsaturated fats (-20.8% relative change).
Between 2002 and 2012, the greatest increase in diet-related cardiometabolic deaths was associated with unprocessed red meats (+14.4% relative change).

evidence.description: Of these, an estimated 318 656 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 306 064-329 755; 45.4%) cardiometabolic deaths per year were associated with suboptimal intakes.
The largest numbers of estimated diet-related cardiometabolic deaths were related to high sodium (66 508 deaths in 2012; 9.5% of all cardiometabolic deaths).
Second largest number of estimated diet-related cardiometabolic deaths was related to low nuts/seeds (59 374; 8.5%).
Third largest number of estimated diet-related cardiometabolic deaths was related to high processed meats (57 766; 8.2%).
Between 2002 and 2012, population-adjusted US cardiometabolic deaths per year decreased by 26.5%.
The greatest decline was associated with insufficient polyunsaturated fats (-20.8% relative change [95% UI, -18.5% to -22.8%]).
The greatest increase was associated with unprocessed red meats (+14.4% [95% UI, 9.1%-19.5%]).

methodologies.name: Comparative Risk Assessment Model
methodologies.description: A comparative risk assessment model combining NHANES dietary survey data, meta-analyses of prospective studies and clinical trials, and national mortality data to estimate disease-specific cardiometabolic deaths attributable to dietary factors.
datasets: National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys (NHANES 1999-2002, 2009-2012)
National Center for Health Statistics mortality data
conditions: Assessment across 10 specific food and nutrient groups

limitations.text: National associations of individual dietary factors with specific cardiometabolic diseases are not well established.
